prerequisites: Minimum knowledge of the core subjects of the degree being pursued (recommended)

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to draft and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering (especially in everything related to the safety and health plan, which must accompany every engineering project).
Ability to direct the activities that are the object of engineering projects, linked in this particular case to the field of occupational risk prevention.

Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, that enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations, always within the field of occupational risk prevention.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, and valuations related to occupational risk prevention in the company.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations and mandatory standards, applying the compliance with said current legislation in the adequate management of occupational risk prevention in a company.
Ability to analyze and assess the social impact of technical solutions.
Ability to organize and plan in the field of business, and other institutions and organizations.

Ability to apply the acquired knowledge in occupational risk prevention and to solve problems in new or unfamiliar environments within broader and multidisciplinary contexts, being able to integrate this knowledge.
Ability for occupational risk prevention and the protection of workers' and users' health and safety.
Adequate knowledge of the concept of a company, the institutional and legal framework of the company; organization and management of companies.
Knowledge and skills to organize and manage projects.
Manage occupational risk prevention in a company by adopting the preventive activity modality that best suits the characteristics of the organization.
Consult legislative references regarding occupational risk prevention in the company.
Handle basic terminology related to general concepts regarding occupational risk prevention in the business world.

Identify the scope of action and basic tools of the three technical preventive disciplines (work safety, industrial hygiene, and applied ergonomics and psychosociology) identifying the differences between them and with occupational medicine (the only non-technical discipline).
Use the main preventive techniques of a company (occupational risk assessment, accident investigation, mainly).

syllabus_topics: Basic concepts and legal framework of reference
Development through Royal Decrees and technical guides
Occupational disease: classification and agents that cause them
Causes and consequences vs Prevention and protection
Planning of prevention in the company
Planning of preventive activity in the company
Safety and health plan or occupational risk prevention management system
Preventive disciplines and modalities of preventive activity
Different modalities of organizing preventive activity
Work equipment and personal protective equipment
Basic techniques for occupational risk prevention
Specific occupational risk assessments (manual handling of loads, data display screens)
Definition and classification of the different branches of industrial hygiene
Agents in the work environment and preventive measures against them
Definition and classification of the different techniques of occupational medicine

assessment_methods.method: Individual basic safety and health study (ESS)
Final exam (EX) for differentiated evaluation / extraordinary call

assessment_rules: The continuous assessment grade is calculated as: 0.1 * ESS + 0.1 * TG + 0.1 * TEST + 0.7 * PORTA. For ordinary evaluation, the formula is 0.1 * ESS + 0.1 * TG + 0.8 * EX. Attendance to more than 80% of classes is mandatory for continuous assessment. The completion and attendance to all practical work presentations are mandatory to pass the course. Students in differentiated evaluation or extraordinary call will be assessed on the theoretical part through a final exam (EX) and must complete and present the two practical works (ESS + TG).
